answer: Rotating juries of five randomly drawn members hold short live video interviews with each applicant; every juror stakes reputation on the verdict. A faker must show a distinct face to a fresh jury each time, so recruiting 100 actors costs 100 paid people while recurring faces get flagged. Jurors who wave a glacier of fakes through lose standing. Draws stay random like karst sinkholes, and a reputation zenith can't buy a jury seat.
